## Why can factor scores have cross-loadings?

A CFA may specify that each item loads on only one factor. That does not
necessarily mean that each *factor score* measures only one factor.
When regression scores are obtained from a model with correlated factors,
the score for one factor generally uses information from indicators of the
other factors as well. In stage 2, the scores can therefore have
cross-loadings and correlated measurement errors.

This vignette shows how `R2spa` accounts for these properties, using
the `PoliticalDemocracy` data from the
[lavaan SEM tutorial](https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/sem.html).
See the [introductory vignette](R2spa.html) for the basic two-stage workflow.

```{r, message=FALSE}
library(lavaan)
library(R2spa)
```

## Scores from a two-factor CFA

First, fit a CFA for industrialization (`ind60`) and political democracy
(`dem60`), both in 1960. `std.lv = TRUE` sets each factor's variance to one
in this measurement model.

```{r}
measurement_model <- '
  ind60 =~ x1 + x2 + x3
  dem60 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4
'
cfa_fit <- cfa(measurement_model, data = PoliticalDemocracy, std.lv = TRUE)
fs_dat <- get_fs(cfa_fit)
head(fs_dat[c("fs_ind60", "fs_dem60")])
```

The score loading matrix describes how the scores relate to the latent
variables. Rows correspond to scores and columns to latent variables.
The off-diagonal entries are *score cross-loadings*, not item cross-loadings
in the original CFA. The error covariance matrix describes the measurement
error remaining in those scores.

```{r}
attr(fs_dat, "fsL")[[1]]
attr(fs_dat, "fsT")[[1]]
```

`tspa()` uses both matrices automatically. The following model estimates
the regression of democracy on industrialization while accounting for the
score cross-loadings and measurement-error covariance:

```{r}
tspa_fit <- tspa("dem60 ~ ind60", data = fs_dat)
standardizedSolution(tspa_fit) |>
  subset(op == "~")
cat(attr(tspa_fit, "tspaModel"))
```

### The score measurement equation

For continuous indicators, regression factor scores have the form

$$
\tilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}} =
\mathbf{A}(\mathbf{y} - \boldsymbol{\mu}) + \boldsymbol{\alpha},
\qquad
\mathbf{A} = \boldsymbol{\Psi}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}^{\top}
\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^{-1},
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Lambda}$ contains the item loadings,
$\boldsymbol{\Psi}$ contains the factor variances and covariances,
$\boldsymbol{\alpha}$ contains the factor means, and
$\boldsymbol{\mu} = \boldsymbol{\nu} +
\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\boldsymbol{\alpha}$ contains the item means.
The model-implied item covariance matrix is
$\boldsymbol{\Sigma} = \boldsymbol{\Lambda}\boldsymbol{\Psi}
\boldsymbol{\Lambda}^{\top} + \boldsymbol{\Theta}$.
In practice, estimated measurement parameters are used in these expressions.

Substituting the CFA equation
$\mathbf{y} = \boldsymbol{\nu} + \boldsymbol{\Lambda}
\boldsymbol{\eta} + \boldsymbol{\varepsilon}$ gives

$$
\tilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}} =
(\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{A}\boldsymbol{\Lambda})\boldsymbol{\alpha}
+ \mathbf{A}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}\boldsymbol{\eta}
+ \mathbf{A}\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}.
$$

Thus, the stage-2 score loadings are
$\mathbf{L} = \mathbf{A}\boldsymbol{\Lambda}$ (`fsL`), the score
intercepts are $\mathbf{b} = (\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{L})
\boldsymbol{\alpha}$ (`fsb`), and the score error covariance is
$\mathbf{T} = \mathbf{A}\boldsymbol{\Theta}\mathbf{A}^{\top}$ (`fsT`).
Even with a simple item-loading pattern, neither $\mathbf{L}$ nor
$\mathbf{T}$ is generally diagonal for regression scores.

## Separate measurement models for each construct

An alternative is to estimate each construct's measurement model separately.
For a simple CFA specification, `local = TRUE` does this in one call. Unlike
the joint CFA above, each score now uses only its own construct's indicators:

```{r}
measurement_3 <- '
  ind60 =~ x1 + x2 + x3
  dem60 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4
  dem65 =~ y5 + y6 + y7 + y8
'
path_model <- '
  dem60 ~ ind60
  dem65 ~ ind60 + dem60
'
fs_local <- get_fs(PoliticalDemocracy, model = measurement_3,
                   std.lv = TRUE, local = TRUE)
attr(fs_local, "fsL")[[1]]
tspa_local <- tspa(path_model, data = fs_local)
standardizedSolution(tspa_local) |>
  subset(op == "~")
```

The combined score loading and error covariance matrices have zero
off-diagonal entries.
These zeros concern the *score measurement model*; the structural relations
among the latent variables are estimated in stage 2.

Separate-model scores need not equal scores from a multi-factor CFA, because
the latter can use information shared across correlated factors. The choice
of stage-1 model should reflect the intended measurement model, including
any substantively justified item cross-loadings or cross-construct residual
covariances.

If a separate model needs additional syntax, such as a within-construct
residual covariance, supply one complete model string per construct:

```{r}
fs_separate <- get_fs(PoliticalDemocracy, local = TRUE,
                      model = c(
                        'ind60 =~ x1 + x2 + x3',
                        'dem60 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4
                         y1 ~~ y4'
                      ))
```

The `local = TRUE` option currently does not compute the joint sampling
covariance needed for `vfsLT = TRUE` and the automated stage-2 standard-error
correction. See [Corrected Standard Errors](corrected-se.html) for other ways
to examine stage-1 estimation uncertainty.

## Combining scores obtained in separate calls

Use `combine_fs()` when constructs have already been scored separately,
including when different measurement software is used. It preserves the
score measurement information needed by the stage-2 functions.

```{r}
fs_ind <- get_fs(PoliticalDemocracy, model = "ind60 =~ x1 + x2 + x3")
fs_dem <- get_fs(PoliticalDemocracy, model = "dem60 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4")
fs_combined <- combine_fs(fs_ind, fs_dem)
tspa_combined <- tspa("dem60 ~ ind60", data = fs_combined)
standardizedSolution(tspa_combined) |>
  subset(op == "~")
```

By default, the inputs must contain the same observations in the same order.
If they include a shared identifier, use `id = "participant_id"` to align
them. `combine_fs()` currently accepts single-group inputs.

The combined measurement matrices retain each input's within-model
loadings and error covariances and set cross-model entries to zero. This
assumes that measurement errors from different input models are uncorrelated.
If cross-construct error covariances are part of the measurement model,
estimate the constructs together instead.
